events.note: On <input> only; on any other tag (input) maps to onInput and the compiler notes it has no standard RN prop.

diagnostics.meaning: A {{ interpolation in a template is never closed with }}.
A "<" in a template is not followed by a tag name.
An element is opened but never closed.
An attribute in a template could not be parsed.
A closing tag appears with no matching opening element.
A closing tag does not match the currently open element.
The *ngFor microsyntax could not be parsed.
A segment of *ngFor microsyntax is not supported and was ignored.

An element carries more than one structural directive (*ngIf, *ngFor, ...); only the first is kept and each later one is dropped. One structural directive per element: nest one element inside the other.
No class decorated with @Component was found in the source file.
The component template could not be resolved (missing inline template and templateUrl).
A CSS selector is not an element or .class selector; the rule was skipped.
A CSS declaration is malformed (expected "property: value").
A CSS property is outside the supported subset; the declaration was dropped.
A spacing, radius or font-size value is off its design-token scale; the generated style uses the nearest on-scale value.
A template tag is not a known Rangular block; it was emitted as <View>.

A field has a non-literal initializer that cannot be emitted verbatim into the generated component (it references this, or the field is assigned in a method); it is declared as undefined there so the output still compiles. A never-assigned non-literal initializer without this (new Date(), Date.now(), an expression over literals) is emitted verbatim and does not warn.
A field is assigned in a method but has a non-literal initializer, so it cannot become useState yet.
*ngIf with else/then microsyntax is not generated yet; the element was emitted unconditionally.
A structural directive other than *ngIf/*ngFor is not supported yet; the element was emitted unconditionally.

A declaration is nested in the wrong parent; option belongs in switcher or select, radio belongs in radio-group, tab belongs in tabs, column belongs in table, step belongs in stepper, menu-item belongs in menu, grid-tile belongs in grid-list, tree-node belongs in tree or another tree-node, nav-item belongs in bottom-nav, row-action belongs in row, timeline-item belongs in timeline, avatar belongs in avatar-group, and crumb belongs in breadcrumbs, and those groups (plus accordion, which takes panels only, and menu, which also takes dividers) accept only their own declarations.
An <icon> names an icon that is not in the Rangular icon set; the JSON form of this diagnostic carries the full valid list in validIcons.
An <icon> element has no name attribute and no [name] binding, so there is nothing to draw.
An <icon> size is off the icon size scale (20, 24, 28); the generated code uses the nearest on-scale size.
ngModel (two-way, [ngModel] or (ngModelChange)) is used on an element other than <input>; in this version ngModel binds text inputs only.
An ngModel binding does not target a plain component field with a literal initial value, so no write-back or validation state could be generated; the value is bound one way.

A formControlName cannot be bound: the input is not inside a <form> with a [formGroup], the control name is not one of the group's controls, or formControlName was written as a [binding] instead of a static attribute.
A [formGroup] binding does not name a field initialised with new FormGroup(...), so the reactive form cannot be wired.

A field initialised with new FormGroup(...) or new FormControl(...) uses a shape the preview cannot evaluate (only literal values, Validators references and validator calls are supported); the generated app runs the initializer as written.

A template uses <router-outlet> or routerLink, or a component injects Router or ActivatedRoute, but no routes file was resolved: the compiler looks for app.routes.ts next to the root component, or the file named by the CLI --routes flag.
A route entry names a component class that is not an @Component class resolved in this compilation.
Two route entries declare the same path; matching tries entries in order, so the first one wins and the later one never renders.

A route entry or routing construct uses an Angular routing feature Rangular does not support yet (child routes, guards, resolvers, lazy loading, nested outlets, routerLink on a component tag), or a route entry is not a plain object literal with a string path.
A <datetime-picker> mode is not one of the three picker modes (date, time, datetime).
A <chart> type is not one of the three chart types (bar, line, pie); the chart would draw bars instead.
An <otp> length is outside the supported 4 to 8; the generated control clamps it to the nearest of the two.
A <datetime-picker> minuteInterval is not 1 or 5; the generated code uses the nearest of the two.
A <sheet>, <dialog>, <menu>, <drawer> or <lightbox> has no [open] binding, so it cannot be opened or closed from the component; it renders statically open.
A tooltip attribute or [tooltip] binding sits on an element that cannot host a tooltip in this version (button, row and icon-button can); the tooltip was dropped.
An event binding holds an assignment statement (for example (close)="sheetOpen = false"); template event bindings take a method call, never an assignment, so the binding was dropped.
A <column> has no name attribute (or key alias) naming the row property it displays, so the table cannot read its cells.
A <slider> range is unusable: min must be below max (an error, checked when both are statically known), and step must be above zero (a warning; the generated code uses 1).
A <progress-bar> value is statically known to sit outside 0 to 100; the generated code clamps it into range.
A <spinner> size is off the icon size scale (20, 24, 28); the generated code uses the nearest on-scale size.
A badge attribute or [badge] binding sits on an element that cannot host a badge in this version (button, row, icon and nav-item can); the badge was dropped.

A class binding Rangular cannot honour was dropped: [class] and [ngClass] bind a whole dynamic class value, which cannot be resolved to StyleSheet entries at compile time, and [class.name] only works when the component styles declare that class and the block takes a style. The supported toggle is [class.name]="cond" over a class declared in the component styles; the other working pattern is named classes in the component styles with the plain class attribute, swapped with *ngIf.

A style binding or static style attribute was dropped: [style], [style.prop] (with or without a unit) and [ngStyle] bind raw CSS values, which bypass the token-snapped component styles, and a static style="..." attribute has no StyleSheet entry to attach to. Styles live in the component styles block under a class, applied with the plain class attribute or toggled with [class.name].

An [attr.x] binding was dropped: it targets an HTML attribute, and React Native elements have no arbitrary attributes. Use the plain attribute when the block supports one, or the specific [prop] binding the block documents.
A statement in a component method is outside the supported translation subset; it was left as a TODO.
A relative import in a compiled file could not be resolved to a source file.
A templateUrl, styleUrl or relative import resolved to a file outside the project root; the file was not read.
Two or more source files import each other in a cycle; the cycle was broken at the repeated file, whose classes were already registered.
Two different component classes declare the same selector in one compilation.

A constructor dependency names a type that is not a known @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }) service in this compilation and not a built-in token (HttpClient, Router / ActivatedRoute in a routed app, or SnackBar in a component).
Injectable services depend on each other in a cycle; container registrations could not be ordered.
Doctor: a hex colour literal appears in the component styles instead of a colour role token.
Doctor: a spacing, radius or font-size value in the styles is off its design-token scale (the compiler would snap it).
Doctor: loose text sits directly inside a container element instead of a text element.
Doctor: an element with a (click) binding is sized below the 44 by 44 minimum tap target.
Doctor: an image element has no declared width and height.
The rangular init command was pointed at a directory that is not empty.
A template uses a pipe that is neither a built-in pipe nor a @Pipe class resolved in this compilation; the JSON form lists the known pipes in the fix.
A static minlength or maxlength attribute value is not a plain number; the validator was dropped instead of emitting the text into generated code.

An attribute directive is outside the supported subset (a bracket selector, @Input fields, an ElementRef, and ngOnInit or setter bodies made only of this.el.nativeElement.style.<prop> assignments), or it is used on a host the subset cannot style; the directive applied no styles.
An <ng-content> carries a select attribute; multi-slot projection is not supported yet, so the element behaves as the default slot and receives all projected children.
The rangular init target name is not a safe directory name (letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen only, and not . or ..); nothing was written.
